correctness.rationale: For even \(n\), central symmetry makes both symmetrizations equal to the polygon. For odd \(n\), with unit circumradius, \(r=\cos(\pi/n)\), \(c=\cos(\pi/(2n))\), and asymmetry \(s=1/r\), polarity gives \(P_n^\circ=s(-P_n)\) and hence \(H_n=rA_n^\circ\). The half-difference body \(A_n\) is a regular \(2n\)-gon of circumradius \(c\) and inradius \(c^2\); its polar is rotated by half a sector with circumradius \(1/c^2\). Therefore the vertices of \(H_n\) lie in side-normal directions of \(A_n\), and the least centered containment factor is \(r/c^4=4s/(s+1)^2\). Opposite contact points saturate a supporting-strip width, which rules out improvement by translation. Independent symbolic reconstruction verified \(r/c^4=4s/(s+1)^2\), and the package polygon checker reconstructs the operations through \(n=51\). The all-\(n\) claim rests on the regular-polygon/polar argument, not the finite replay.
residual_risks: The equality family is Euclidean-regular up to affine invariance; no classification of all equality cases is claimed.
